name: Teledyne Technologies
description: Teledyne makes sensors, cameras and instruments for demanding environments: digital imaging (visible, infrared and X-ray sensors and cameras, plus MEMS and semiconductors), marine, environmental and test-and-measurement instruments, aerospace and defense electronics, and engineered systems for NASA and the Department of War. About a quarter of sales (25.5 percent) go to the US government, mostly fixed-price contracts; the rest are commercial instruments and components sold to industrial, scientific and medical customers. Teledyne grows by acquiring technology niches (about $270M of 2025 sales came from acquisitions).

businessLines.name: Digital Imaging
businessLines.how: Sells sensors, cameras, thermal-imaging cores, X-ray detectors, MEMS and high-reliability semiconductors to industrial machine-vision, scientific, medical, space and defense customers: product sales, often designed into the customer's system, plus some contract engineering and manufacturing services. $645.5M of the segment's sales were to the US government.

businessLines.name: Instrumentation
businessLines.how: Sells marine instruments and underwater vehicles, environmental and laboratory analysers, gas and flame detectors, and electronic test and measurement gear (oscilloscopes, protocol analyzers) to navies, offshore energy, labs, plants and electronics designers: one-time instrument sales plus parts and service.

businessLines.name: Aerospace and Defense Electronics
businessLines.how: Sells high-reliability electronic and optical components and subsystems, avionics data and connectivity systems, interconnects and aviation batteries to aircraft, radar, electronic-warfare, space and satellite programmes: contracted production for primes, mostly fixed-price, plus commercial airline data services.

businessLines.name: Engineered Systems
businessLines.how: Government contract work: systems engineering, integration and advanced technology development for NASA, the Department of War and the Department of Energy, plus electrochemical energy systems and specialty military electronics. $368.3M of sales were to the US government, so it is almost entirely government-funded.

whatsNext.when: January 2026; implementation by the Secretary of War pending
whatsNext.text: Executive order (January 2026) restricting stock buybacks and dividends by 'major defense contractors'; the 10-K says it is unclear whether and how it applies to Teledyne and that it could materially affect Teledyne's ability to repurchase stock or pay dividends
